notes: Curated list of the data issues found by the 6 Nov 2026 audit (data accuracy and freshness, frontend and backend reports). Counts, column names and office codes only; no personal data. Keep statuses current: docs/data-quality.md, 'Audit findings'. auto_check names the matching check of vm/sync/lib/quality (rules.js / checks.js / store.js); the API attaches its live state from quality.json.

findings.title: Withheld served a partial copy (45,600 of 66,760 rows)
findings.summary: The VM copied the Withheld sheet while an upload was still writing it, stored only the first 45,600 rows and kept serving that copy. The cheap version check reads only the header and first row, so the copy would have stayed short for up to 6 hours.
findings.evidence: Copy of 06:36 UTC: 45,600 rows and column scn_witheld_date gone; live sheet at 06:47: 66,760 rows (11.26 MB against 7.43 MB). Page: 45,600 withheld vs 66,760; 'No valid reason' 17,688 vs 23,638; Domestic 37,150 vs 54,131. The old quality hook still scored the dataset 99.
findings.impact: Withheld showed about 21,000 fewer applications than the sheet, and every breakdown on the page was short by about a third. The unscored rating metric nsc_withheld_network_share was built from the short copy.
findings.cause: Sync: the upload clears the tab and appends chunks; the sync read it mid-way, and the version peek (A1:Z2) did not change as later chunks landed, so the full copy was not read again until the 6-hour maximum skip.
findings.fix: Done: hold back a copy with many fewer rows or lost columns (3.49). Still worth doing: include the row count or the upload's uploadedAt in the version check, and lower maxSkipHours for nsc_pending and withheld to 1.
findings.status_note: Since 3.49 the sync holds back a new copy that has lost columns and more than 20% of its rows (vm/sync/lib/holdback.js), keeps serving the previous copy and reads the source again on the next run. The 6 Nov copy would have been held. The version peek itself is unchanged.
findings.auto_unit: copy held or short|copies held or short

findings.title: REM defaulters shows ₹0 outstanding and "As on —"
findings.summary: Since the 5 Nov upload, the column the page reads for the amount (NOTOSD_UPD) and for the date (UPD_DT) is 0 in every row of all three REM dumps, so the page shows ₹0 for every defaulter and no report date.
findings.evidence: 18,419 rows across the three dumps with NOTOSD_UPD = 0 and UPD_DT = 0 (one shifted row aside, AF-09). NOTOSD still holds amounts (₹8.97 Cr in Ind/Com). The page showed ₹55.51 Cr for 16,573 consumers as on 26 Oct on 1–2 Nov.
findings.impact: Every amount on REM defaulters is ₹0 and the header says "As on —".
findings.cause: Source export changed (NOTOSD_UPD and UPD_DT no longer filled); the page has no fallback (rem/defaulters.html reads only notosd_upd and upd_dt).
findings.fix: App: fall back to NOTOSD (or OSD) when NOTOSD_UPD is 0 or blank, take the date from the dump date, and warn when the total is 0 but there are rows. Source sheet: ask the owner of the REM dump whether the export changed.
findings.status_note: Fixed in 3.55: rem/defaulters.html falls back to OSD, then NOTOSD, when the update amount and date are 0. All counts unchanged; amounts and the "As on" date are back. The source export still leaves NOTOSD_UPD at 0, so the automatic check keeps flagging the sheet.

findings.title: Withheld full sync runs at its 240 s time limit
findings.summary: A full read of Withheld took 238 s against the 240 s limit for frequent sources, and the sheet is now about 50% larger, so the next full read is likely to time out and be retried every few minutes.
findings.evidence: Run of 06:36 UTC: 238 s against DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS.frequent = 240 s, mostly the PocketBase write of about 45,000 rows; the live sheet has about 21,000 more rows. Next longest: rem_defaulters_ind_com 243 s of 600 s.
findings.impact: A timed-out run leaves PocketBase partial and the run log in error, and every 5 minutes repeats a 4-minute download and write on the 1 GB VM. The page itself recovers because the snapshot is published before the database write.
findings.cause: Sync: withheld and nsc_pending have no timeoutMs of their own in vm/sync/sources/google.js.
findings.fix: Set timeoutMs: 10 * 60000 on nsc_pending and withheld in vm/sync/sources/google.js.
findings.status_note: No timeoutMs on either source in google.js yet.

findings.title: Unbilled Sep–Nov 2026 read live, not mirrored
findings.summary: The three newest unbilled months (Sep-2026, Oct-2026, NOV-26), the ones users care about, have no VM copy: Important data sheets reads them straight from Google, and the Sources tab does not list them.
findings.evidence: important_unbilled_months (Supabase) lists 11 months; the sync's important_unbilled_* sources are hard-coded to Jan–Aug 2026. In mirror mode the page made 17 Google requests while the Sources tab lists 7 live tabs.
findings.impact: The newest months load slowly or fail when Google is slow, and Sources understates what the page reads live.
findings.cause: Sync: the month list is editable in the app, but the sync's list in google.js is fixed.
findings.fix: Generate the important_unbilled_* sources from important_unbilled_months at sync time, or list the extra months as live in lib/sources_live.js. Normalise the label NOV-26 to Nov-2026.
findings.status_note: google.js still lists Jan–Aug 2026 only.

findings.title: 10 sources are months old at the source
findings.summary: The VM copies are current, but the sheets themselves have not been updated for months, so these reports show old data. Seven of them feed the Performance index, where those parameters are marked stale and drop out.
findings.evidence: Newest date in the data: accidents 2025-06-21, docket KPI 2025-06-30, O&M advance 2025-07-31, smart meter work orders 2025-11-12, DD summary 2026-01-14, weekly 2026-02-23, historical NSC 2026-03-08, safety 2026-03-25, peak load 2026-05-06, feeder outage 2026-08-31.
findings.impact: Pages look current (the copy is minutes old) while their numbers are up to 16 months old; Sources shows no 'as on' date.
findings.cause: Source sheets are no longer being updated.
findings.fix: Ask each sheet owner to paste or upload the latest report, or retire the report. Show the source's 'as on' date on the Sources tab.
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (source.stale) for every dataset with a date column; Docket KPI has no date column, so its age is not detected.
findings.auto_unit: source old at the origin|sources old at the origin

findings.title: Collection: ₹699 Cr booked to region office codes (10 divisions, 44 CCCs shown)
findings.summary: Payments booked to the three region office codes are counted as extra divisions and CCCs, so the page shows 10 divisions and 44 CCCs where the zone has 7 and 41.
findings.evidence: 1,845 rows, ₹699.06 Cr of ₹4,503 Cr (15.5%), on codes 6610000, 6620000 and 6630000. The page names them '<region> bulk'.
findings.impact: Division and CCC counts are wrong, and the division and CCC tables carry three 'bulk' rows that are not offices.
findings.cause: Source sheet books HT / bulk payments at region level; the page treats each region code as a division and a CCC.
findings.fix: Show region-office codes as a separate 'Region office (HT / bulk)' bucket and leave them out of the division and CCC counts. The rating already leaves them out.
findings.status_note: collection.html still counts the '<region> bulk' rows as divisions and CCCs. Detected automatically since 3.49 (collection.office_codes).

findings.title: Losses: region and zone rows hold 725 MU that no division or CCC carries
findings.summary: The region and zone rows of the Loss sheet carry about 725 MU (19%) of input energy that is in no division or CCC row, so zone AT&C is lower than every division's and is not their weighted mean.
findings.evidence: Sep 2026 cumulative: zone input 3,793.51 MU, sum of the 41 CCC rows 3,068.13 MU. Zone AT&C 22.35%; divisions 22.2–33.2%; AT&C from the CCC rows 26.60%.
findings.impact: Zone and region AT&C on Losses and in the Performance index look better than any division, and nothing on the page explains why.
findings.cause: Source sheet: input energy (probably HT / bulk) is booked only at region level.
findings.fix: Ask the Loss sheet owner what the extra input is; add a note on the Losses page (and the rating's methodology), or add the missing rows.
findings.status_note: No note on loss.html yet. Detected automatically since 3.49 (loss.rollup, in MU).

findings.title: IDs and amounts destroyed by scientific notation (471 solar, 6 theft, 1 pending MC)
findings.summary: Cells were saved as rounded scientific notation, so the real application numbers and amounts are lost and cannot be recovered from the copy.
findings.evidence: solar_connections APPLICATION_NO: 471 cells (422 as 6.00E+09, 49 as 4.00E+09), plus 77 '(null)'; theft_assessment PAYMENT AMT: 6 cells (3 significant figures); pending_mc LOAD: 1 cell.
findings.impact: Solar applications cannot be looked up or de-duplicated by number; six theft payments are rounded.
findings.cause: Source sheet: the column is formatted as a number before export.
findings.fix: Format the columns as plain text in the sheet and re-export.
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (number.scientific).

findings.title: Shifted REM Ind/Com row puts a date in OSD (16.6% of the column)
findings.summary: One row of the REM Ind/Com dump has its columns shifted, so a date (20261103) sits in OSD and is read as ₹2.03 Cr.
findings.evidence: 1 row (CCC 6621103, row 4430 of the copy): OSD 20261103, NOTOSD 'NO'. That one value is 16.6% of the OSD column total.
findings.impact: Any total over OSD for Ind/Com is overstated by ₹2.03 Cr.
findings.cause: Source sheet: a tab or line break inside an address cell shifted the row.
findings.fix: Fix the row in the source. The page should ignore rows whose NOTOSD is not a number.
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (value.date_in_number).

findings.title: Sources tab overstates freshness
findings.summary: For sources whose change check is a cheap peek or a meta file, 'Every 5 min' and a 5-minute-old check time suggest the content is 5 minutes fresh, but the content is re-read only when the peek changes or every 6 to 24 hours.
findings.evidence: NSC and Withheld: only A1:Z2 is read every 5 minutes; full read on change or every 6 h. Storage reports: keyed on meta.json, full read every 24 h (fetchedAt was 18–20 h old). The tab showed the partial Withheld copy as ok and fresh. Accident reports showed 'changed 1 Nov' for June 2025 content.
findings.impact: Admins trust a copy that may be hours old, or short, because the tab says it was checked minutes ago.
findings.cause: App: the tab leads with the check time and does not name the version method or the source's 'as on' date.
findings.fix: Show 'content last read' next to 'checked', name the version method (peek, meta, ETag), raise a status when a full re-read is overdue, and show the source's 'as on' date.
findings.status_note: Since 3.49 a held copy shows as 'Held' instead of ok, so the worst case is visible. The peek and the 'checked' emphasis are unchanged.

findings.title: Meter master: 6,638 copied rows
findings.summary: The meter master holds thousands of exact duplicate rows and repeated consumer IDs.
findings.evidence: 6,638 full-row duplicates; 6,903 repeated CON_ID values, of 288,888 rows.
findings.impact: Counts of meters in use can be overstated unless the page counts distinct consumers.
findings.cause: Source sheet export.
findings.fix: De-duplicate at export; the page should count distinct CON_ID for 'used'.
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (row.duplicate; key.duplicate on CON_ID).

findings.title: Repeated IDs in safety inspections and highway crossings
findings.summary: IDs that should be unique repeat: Inspection ID in the safety app (one row per finding is plausible, but some rows are exact copies) and the crossing ID in the highway crossings sheet.
findings.evidence: safety_inspection: 1,951 repeated Inspection IDs, 160 full-row copies. highway_crossings: 245 repeated IDs, 43 full-row copies.
findings.impact: Counts of inspections and crossings can include duplicates; a crossing cannot be identified by its ID.
findings.cause: Source sheet: IDs are not enforced as unique.
findings.fix: Make crossing IDs unique at source; drop the exact copies in the safety sheet.
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (key.duplicate; safety repeats are info only).

findings.title: Other repeated IDs (meter ISU, CRM, ERP, theft, defective)
findings.summary: Smaller numbers of repeated consumer IDs and meter serials in other dumps.
findings.evidence: meter_isu CON_ID 1,185; meter_crm CON_ID 59 (+1 full row); meter_erp Serial Number 103; theft_assessment Consumer ID 32; defective_details CON_ID 60.
findings.impact: 'Issued' and similar counts can be a little high unless pages count distinct values.
findings.cause: Source exports (repeat assessments may be legitimate).
findings.fix: Confirm repeat assessments or merge them; count distinct serials and consumers on the pages.
findings.status_note: Only meter_erp has a key configured (key.duplicate on serial_number); meter_isu, meter_crm, theft and defective repeats are not checked automatically.

findings.title: Collection: 80 same-day CCC duplicates in Nov 2024 (₹3.38 Cr)
findings.summary: For 20–30 Nov 2024 the sheet has two rows for the same date, CCC and payment mode, with different values.
findings.evidence: 80 groups of (PAYMENT_DT, CCC_CODE, MODE), all 20–30 Nov 2024; ₹3.38 Cr if counted twice.
findings.impact: Collection for late Nov 2024 may be double-counted.
findings.cause: Source sheet: those days were probably pasted twice.
findings.fix: Confirm with the owner and re-export those days.
findings.status_note: Not checked automatically (no composite key rule).

findings.title: Loss report: all of 2023 doubled
findings.summary: Every 2023 month has each CCC twice, and one CCC appears twice in Jan–Mar 2025.
findings.evidence: 560 rows: 82 CCC rows a month for 2023; 7 pairs with conflicting values.
findings.impact: None on the page today (it keeps the last row per CCC and month), but any other reader would double-count 2023.
findings.cause: Source sheet.
findings.fix: Delete the duplicate 2023 block.
findings.status_note: Harmless to Losses as it is built today; not checked automatically.

findings.title: A few copied rows in Capex, ICDS, DD summary and peak load
findings.summary: Small numbers of rows that are exact copies of an earlier row.
findings.evidence: capex_details 4, icds_a 4, icds_a_plus 4, dd_summary 1, dtr_peak_load 2.
findings.impact: Totals are off by a row or two.
findings.cause: Source sheet.
findings.fix: Remove the copies at source.
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (row.duplicate).

findings.title: Impossible and future dates (9982, 0204, 0206, 20256)
findings.summary: Typing errors in date columns give years that cannot be right, or dates in the future.
findings.evidence: dd_summary Dis Date: 4 future, 11 before 1990, 27 #NUM!, 559 in a second format (e.g. 9982-09-12, 0204-02-15). icds_a_plus METER INSTALL DATE: 5 future, 1 in year 206, 14 unreadable (e.g. 0206-10-13, 12.10.20256). meter_crm SERV_CONN_DATE: 1 future. nsc_pending INSPECTION_DATE: 1 future.
findings.impact: These rows fall outside date filters and age buckets, or are aged wrongly.
findings.cause: Source sheet: hand-typed dates.
findings.fix: Correct the typos and use one date format per column.

findings.title: 1900–1912 placeholder connection dates in the REM dumps (643 rows)
findings.summary: DATE_OF_CO holds spreadsheet placeholder dates (1900–1912) instead of a blank.
findings.impact: Connection age is shown as over a century for these consumers.
findings.cause: Source export fills unknown dates with a placeholder.
findings.fix: Leave unknown dates blank at source; pages should treat dates before 1950 as unknown.
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (date.placeholder, info).

findings.title: 170 negative loan balances in PM Surya Ghar
findings.summary: Outstanding Amount (INR), a loan balance, is negative in 170 rows.
findings.evidence: pmsgy_malda 45, pmsgy_uttar_dinajpur 96, pmsgy_dakshin_dinajpur 29 (e.g. -229000).
findings.impact: Total outstanding loans are understated.
findings.cause: Source sheet: sign error.
findings.fix: Correct the sign at source.
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (number.negative on outstanding_amount_inr).

findings.title: 8 highway-crossing coordinates lost their decimal point
findings.summary: Latitude or longitude was stored with comma grouping and no decimal point, e.g. 24,870,257.0000000 for 24.870257.
findings.evidence: 7 latitudes and 8 longitudes. The automatic check, which also catches points outside the zone, finds 22 rows off the map.
findings.impact: Those crossings are missing from the map or plotted far away.
findings.cause: Source sheet.
findings.fix: Enter decimal degrees (about 24.3–26.8 N, 87.3–89.4 E) and reject out-of-range values in the form.
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (geo.range).

findings.title: DTR category mix shows everything as "Other"
findings.summary: The DTR page expects category codes ND, AG, IND and DTC, but the sheet uses other codes (such as R), so the Load category mix counts every DTR as Other and the Agriculture and Industrial filters return nothing.
findings.evidence: Frontend audit F-15: dtr/index.html matches 'ND', 'AG', 'IND', 'DTC'; all 40,429 DTRs land in Other.
findings.impact: Load category mix, the Agriculture/Industrial filters and the per-capacity Agri/Ind columns are all zero.
findings.cause: App: the page's code list does not match the sheet.
findings.fix: Map the sheet's category codes to the page's categories (or show the sheet's own codes).
findings.status_note: Fixed in 3.55: dtr/index.html reads the sheet's own category codes (Rural / Mixed / Urban); all other DTR figures unchanged.

findings.title: DD visit shows "Visited 0" for every consumer
findings.summary: The DD visit page showed 0 visited of 10,251 consumers and an empty visit history. Visits come from an Apps Script; when that call fails the page silently shows no visits, so a failure cannot be told apart from 'nobody visited'.
findings.evidence: Parity runs: Visited 0, Not visited 10,251, Visit History 0. pullRemote() in dd/dd_visit.html swallows errors.
findings.impact: Coverage and recovered amounts read as zero; field work is invisible if the script call fails.
findings.cause: Unknown: either no visits are recorded in the script's store, or the script call fails; the page does not say which.
findings.fix: Show a warning when the visit history cannot be loaded, and confirm with the DD team whether visits are being recorded.
findings.status_note: The page still ignores a failed visit-history call. Not checked automatically (sensitive data, no snapshot).

findings.title: Regions named Raiganj and Balurghat instead of Uttar and Dakshin Dinajpur
findings.summary: Reports labelled the Uttar Dinajpur and Dakshin Dinajpur regions by their division towns (Raiganj, Balurghat), and some sheets spell them D DAINAJPUR / U DAINAJPUR, so the same region appeared under different names.
findings.evidence: Performance index regions: Malda, Balurghat, Raiganj (the audit's rating run). Office codes 6620000 and 6630000.
findings.impact: Region names did not match the official names, and a region could be confused with its division of the same name.
findings.cause: App: lib/offices.js used the old region names.
findings.fix: Use Malda, Uttar Dinajpur and Dakshin Dinajpur everywhere and read the old names and typos as aliases.
findings.status_note: Fixed in 3.48: regions show as Uttar Dinajpur and Dakshin Dinajpur; old names and the DAINAJPUR typos are read on the server, in user scopes and in Ask.

findings.title: Smart meter status and ICDS rows with no office
findings.summary: Many rows cannot be placed in any region, division or CCC, so they drop out of office filters and breakdowns.
findings.evidence: smart_meter_status: 519 rows (5.4%) with no office at all, 1,430 without CCC. icds_a: 922 of 3,538 (26%) with no division or CCC (DISTRICT variants).
findings.impact: Office-level numbers on these pages are short; the rows count only in the zone total.
findings.cause: Source sheet: CCC not filled.
findings.fix: Fill ccc_final (smart meter) and add a CCC column (ICDS) at source; add aliases where the DISTRICT text is consistent.
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (office.blank).

findings.title: Rows from other states and unknown offices (PM Surya Ghar, O&M, upkeeping)
findings.summary: Some rows name offices outside WBSEDCL or codes not in the office list, or leave the division blank.
findings.evidence: pmsgy_*: 5 sub-divisions from other states, 36 region/division mismatches. onm_advance: 5 unknown cost centres (e.g. C220000000); costcenter: 1 (C366000100). substation_upkeeping: Division blank in 7 of 21.
findings.impact: These rows land in 'Unmapped' or in the wrong office.
findings.cause: Source sheet: the portal export includes non-WBSEDCL rows; the upkeeping form does not require a division.
findings.fix: Filter non-WBSEDCL rows from the PM Surya Ghar export; add the cost centres to OLD_COST_CENTRES or fix them; make Division mandatory in the upkeeping form.
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (office.unknown, office.mismatch, office.blank).

findings.title: Statewide rows in zone sheets (WRIDD, accidents)
findings.summary: The WRIDD and accident sheets hold rows from other circles; the pages filter them out correctly.
findings.evidence: wridd_schemes: 119 of 236 rows outside the zone (117 in zone, matches the page). accident_reports: 1,135 of 1,631 victim rows outside the zone (438 accidents in zone, matches the page).
findings.impact: None on the pages; larger downloads and room for error in any other reader.
findings.cause: Source sheets are statewide.
findings.fix: Keep the WRIDD sheet zone-only if its owner agrees; nothing needed on the pages.
findings.status_note: The pages already filter to the zone.

findings.title: Other negative values (theft bills, NSC delay, upkeeping score)
findings.summary: A few values below zero where they should not be, and DD summary credits written in accounting brackets.
findings.evidence: theft_assessment Provsnl Bill Amt 6, Provsnl Bill Unit 1; nsc_pending DelayInQtn 1 (-1); substation_upkeeping score 1 (-1); dd_summary OSD 198 negative plus 1,414 in brackets such as (0.37).
findings.impact: Small effects on totals; bracketed DD summary credits are read as text, not as negatives.
findings.cause: Source sheet entries; brackets are an accounting format.
findings.fix: Check the reversals and fix the -1 entries; read brackets as negative (or export plain numbers).
findings.status_note: Detected automatically since 3.49 (number.negative).

findings.title: Sheet errors and blanks in lookup columns (#N/A, (null), legend rows)
findings.summary: Formula errors and placeholder text sit where values should be, and the PM Surya Ghar tabs count a legend row as an application.
findings.evidence: disconnection: PAID DATE and PAID AMOUNT #N/A in 23,437 rows, DISCONNECTION DATE in 15,861, 4 blank headers. onm_advance: 8 #N/A. important_unbilled_aug_2026: 6 #N/A in each of col_k, col_n, col_q. puja_hourly_load_2025: 2 errors in each of 9 columns. pending_mc: CON_ID (null) 7, COLL_DATE (null) 62. pmsgy_*: 1 legend row each (3).
findings.impact: Disconnection shows 'no action' for lookup misses; PM Surya Ghar counts three extra applications.
findings.cause: Source sheet lookups and a second header row.
findings.fix: Wrap lookups in IFERROR (blank), drop the legend row, export blanks instead of (null).

findings.auto_unit: dataset with text or errors in number columns|datasets with text or errors in number columns

findings.title: Units and formats: lakh not in the header, mixed date formats, ₹90 lakh subsidy
findings.summary: Small format problems that invite mistakes: an amount in lakh with no unit, date columns mixing two formats, and one subsidy far above the scheme's cap.
findings.evidence: collection_report AMOUNT PAID is in ₹ lakh with no unit in the header (the page and rating read it correctly). solar_connections: 7 date columns mix ISO and dd/mm/yyyy (up to 3,325 rows per column). pmsgy_malda: 1 Eligible Subsidy Amount of ₹90,00,000 for a 5,000 kW proposal (typical ₹78,000).
findings.impact: None today on the pages for the units; the subsidy outlier inflates the subsidy total.
findings.cause: Source sheets.
findings.fix: Add the unit to the header; one date format per column; correct or exclude the subsidy above the scheme cap.
findings.status_note: Not checked automatically.

findings.title: PRT oil tests sheet is empty
findings.summary: The oil test sheet has a header and no rows, so the PRT page has no test records although its status is OK.
findings.evidence: prt_oil_tests: 0 rows at source (header only).
findings.impact: PRT shows no oil tests.
findings.cause: Source sheet: no tests entered yet.
findings.fix: Confirm with the PRT team whether tests are being entered elsewhere.
findings.status_note: Allowed to be empty in rules.js (allowEmpty), so no automatic warning.

findings.title: Nightly refresh skipped after an early-morning check
findings.summary: A daily source checked between midnight and 02:00 IST (a retry or a write-through) counts as 'checked today', so that night's 02:00 refresh is skipped, while Sources marks it overdue.
findings.evidence: Backend audit M9: for a daily source last checked at 00:30 IST, isDue (vm/sync/lib/schedule.js) skips until 02:00 IST the next day; nextDue (lib/sources_info.js) expects 02:00 the same day.
findings.impact: A daily report can be a day older than it should be, and Sources disagrees with the sync.
findings.cause: Sync: two different 'due' rules.
findings.fix: In isDue, make a daily source due when its last check was before 02:00 IST of the current IST day; share one function with sources_info.js.
findings.status_note: schedule.js unchanged.

findings.title: A user's write can seem to vanish while a sync runs
findings.summary: After a write in the app, the page reads the new data only while a 3-minute 'dirty' mark lasts. If the refresh waits behind a longer sync, or a deploy restarts the app, the page shows the old copy again until the next scheduled sync.
findings.evidence: Backend audit M7: DIRTY_MAX_MS = 3 min (lib/mirror.js); syncs of 4–7 min seen; 9 deploys on 6 Nov, each killing pending write-through refreshes.
findings.impact: Users see their change disappear for up to an hour on hourly sources.
findings.cause: Sync: the dirty mark expires before the write-through finishes, and pending refreshes are not persisted.
findings.fix: Keep the dataset dirty until the refresh ends; persist pending write-through keys and re-queue them at start.
findings.status_note: lib/mirror.js unchanged.

findings.title: Structure edits on the VM are undone by the next deploy
findings.summary: Admin → Structure writes data/structure.csv inside the release folder, and every deploy unpacks the git copy, so edits silently revert.
findings.evidence: Backend audit M1: server.js writes data/structure.csv in the release; deploy.sh copies data/ with cp -an, which never overwrites the new release's tracked file. About 9 deploys a day.
findings.impact: Estimate structures go back to the git version without a message.
findings.cause: App: runtime data kept inside the release.
findings.fix: Keep structure.csv in the server's data folder (MZO_FILES_DIR), or refuse edits on the VM; write to a temp file and rename.
findings.status_note: server.js still writes data/structure.csv next to the code.

findings.title: Edited datasets can keep stray rows or a stale page copy
findings.summary: Two editor races: returning a dataset to its original while a large save is still applying can leave stray rows in the VM copy, and a save whose answer was lost can report 'Nothing was saved' and leave the page's copy stale.
findings.evidence: Backend audit M3 (release() takes neither the sync lock nor the per-dataset chain) and M4 (a replayed committed batch skips afterCommit).
findings.impact: Pages can show rows that are not in the source, or miss an edit, until the dataset changes again.
findings.cause: App: editor commit and mode switch are not serialised with the sync.
findings.fix: Run release() inside the dataset's exclusive chain and hold the sync lock; regenerate the snapshot on a replay of a committed batch.
findings.status_note: lib/editor unchanged since the audit.
